we have developed and demonstrated a method that can measure the single-particle linewidth of an ensemble with a high degree of statistical significance, and that this method has revealed that the single-particle spectral linewidth of nanomaterials can be controlled synthetically, and that this control has not yet been achieved for many materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ensemble linewidths are not necessarily indicative of single-emitter spectral linewidths, and that synthetic control of single-particle linewidth is a necessary step in the optimization of nanocrystal materials.
ensemble spectral linewidths are determined by a complex interplay between single-particle linewidth variations and inhomogeneity in a sample, and that these factors can be independently tuned.
ensemble spectral linewidths are not a reliable metric of single-particle linewidth, and thus, single-particle linewidth is a more accurate metric of nanocrystal quality.
